title: Operate NEXXUS
summary: Learn the control room itself: modes, the command bar, the guardrails and how to read what the system is doing. Every step uses something that really exists in NEXXUS.

modules.title: Find your way around
modules.goal: Know where everything is and what the system is telling you.

steps.title: Meet the Modes menu
steps.why: NEXXUS behaves differently in each mode. Conversation only talks; build modes build; Diagnostic watches the machinery. Knowing the mode is knowing what will happen when you type.
do: Open the Modes menu in the bottom bar and read every entry.
Switch to Diagnostic (Boiler Room) and look at the engine lights on the left.

commands.label: Ask the Boiler Room
commands.text: which engines are answering right now?
commands.where: NEXXUS command bar, in Diagnostic mode

tips: The mode banner above the command bar always says which mode you are in.
A restart always returns NEXXUS to Conversation, on purpose.
steps.check: You can name three modes and say what each is for.

steps.title: Use the command cheat sheet and the Prompt Recipe Vault
steps.why: You never have to memorise commands. The cheat sheet lists what NEXXUS understands, and the vault holds proven build prompts.
do: Press the [i] button next to the search box and type what you want to do in plain words.
Press [P] to open the Prompt Recipe Vault and open one recipe.
tips: Typing 'help' or 'commands' in the cheat sheet search finds the basics.
A line you click is put in the command box but not sent: you stay in control.
steps.check: You found a command you did not know and can say what it does.

modules.title: Talk, make and think
modules.goal: Use Conversation, Creation and Sketch modes for what each does best.

steps.title: See why building is a deliberate choice
steps.why: In Conversation mode a build request is halted and you are asked to pick a build mode. This is a safety feature: nothing is built by accident.
do: Type a build request and read the reply that stops it.

commands.label: A request that will be halted
commands.text: build me a landing page for a coffee shop
commands.where: NEXXUS command bar, in Conversation mode

tips: A plain question like 'how do I build a funnel?' is just conversation; an order is what gets halted.
steps.check: NEXXUS asked you to pick a build mode instead of building.

steps.title: Make a visual in Creation mode
steps.why: Creation mode turns a description into one picture or animated page you can see straight away, with no project to manage.
do: Describe a logo or badge for something you care about.
Look at the result in the artifact panel and refine it with a second message.

prompts.label: A first logo
prompts.text: Make a simple, bold logo for a small project called <name>. Two colours, a clean shape, readable at small size.

prompts.label: Refine it
prompts.text: Keep the shape, make the colours calmer, and add a subtle shadow.

tips: Say what it is for and who will see it: a good brief beats a long one.
Change one thing at a time when refining.
steps.check: You made a visual and changed it at least once.

steps.title: Think it through in Sketch mode
steps.why: Before you build, sketch the idea: pick a domain, state a hypothesis, dig in and reach a thesis. Nothing is built and nothing rushes you.
do: Pick a domain you want to work in and state one hypothesis about what people need there.
Follow the suggestion pills until you have a one-paragraph thesis.

prompts.label: A hypothesis to start from
prompts.text: I think <who> struggle with <problem> because <reason>, and a small tool that <does what> would help.

tips: A good hypothesis can be wrong. That is its job.
Write down what would change your mind.
steps.check: You have a thesis you could explain in two sentences.

modules.title: Stay safe and share what you learn
modules.goal: Understand the guardrails, then teach by sharing.

steps.title: Read the guardrails
steps.why: NEXXUS keeps outside code staged until you approve it, signs what it trusts and reports drift. Knowing this is what lets you use it without fear.
do: Open the System Specs button and read the Grid Controller and AXIS-Bridge sections.
Open PERIMETER in the control dock and find Hard Lock and Quarantine.
tips: Hard Lock freezes a node and is lifted only with the admin token.
Anything that adds capability waits for the owner's approval.
steps.check: You can explain, in your own words, what Hard Lock does and why tools are staged.

steps.title: Build your profile
steps.why: Your profile wall is how others will know what you build. A name, a headline and an about section are the minimum.
do: Add your name and headline, then write your About section.

prompts.label: Draft your About
prompts.text: Help me write a three-sentence About for a builder who is learning <skill> and wants to build <goal>. Plain, honest, no hype.

tips: Say what you are learning, not what you wish you were.
steps.check: Your name, headline and About are filled in.

steps.title: Share what you learned, publicly
steps.why: Teaching is how you learn it twice. A short public post about what you just did helps the next person, and it is the first step toward mentoring.
do: Write a post on the floor about one thing you learned in this track (at least a couple of sentences).
Press the 'private' tag under it so it becomes public.

prompts.label: A good shape for the post
prompts.text: Today I learned <one thing>. I tried <what I did>. It worked / did not work because <reason>. Next I will try <next step>.

tips: Keep it PG-13 and keep private details out.
steps.check: You have a public post of at least 40 characters.
